title: 2001 HMMT February Algebra Problem 7
statement: A polynomial \(P\) has four roots, \(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}, 2,4\). The product of the roots is 1 , and \(P(1)=1\). Find \(P(0)\).

solutions.text: A polynomial \(Q\) with \(n\) roots, \(x_{1}, \ldots, x_{n}\), and \(Q\left(x_{0}\right)=1\) is given by \(Q(x)=\) \(\frac{\left(x-x_{1}\right)\left(x-x_{2}\right) \cdots\left(x-x_{n}\right)}{\left(x_{0}-x_{1}\right)\left(x_{0}-x_{2}\right) \cdots\left(x_{0}-x_{4}\right)}\), so \(P(0)=\frac{1}{\frac{3}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot(-1) \cdot(-3)}=\frac{8}{9}\).
